title: Rabbah bar Shimi (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as Ravina’s student, citing [Kiddushin 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.45b.1), where the Rabbis said to Ravina, “But perhaps…”; Rabbah bar Shimi said to them: “The Master said explicitly that he does not hold this of Rav,” etc. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Kiddushin.45b.1.3) identifies “the Master” as Ravina. Hyman cites [Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Kiddushin.45b.7.1), the She’iltot and Tosafot Rid for that interpretation. Likewise in [Pesachim 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.6b.5) he speaks in Ravina’s name.

He is likewise mentioned in [Megillah 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.24a.14) after Rav Papa, giving the reason why the one who reads the haftarah from the Prophets leads the Shema: because they would come to quarrel. Hyman therefore considers Yuchasin correct in saying that there were two Rabbah bar Shimis, against [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3186&lang=en).[^3]

notes.text: Hyman attributes the Master identification to the named commentators and concludes that there were two homonyms. “After Rav Papa” can describe the sequence in the cited text; no extra generational inference is added.

Davidson Kiddushin 45b reads Rabbah bar Shimi’s explicit statement, and consulted Vilna Rashi explains Mar as Ravina. Tosafot/She’iltot/Tosafot Rid and Yuchasin/Seder HaDorot exact claims remain separately attributed. “After Rav Papa” does not alone establish a generation.

The linked Tosafot credits Rashi with the identification and cites the She’iltot for ruling like Ravina. Heilprin asks what proves there were two sages named Rabbah bar Shimi and allows that one man may have lived a long life.
